item.title: 400M+ views writing LinkedIn for 100+ founders. what actually works: 1. post from the foun…
item.description:
400M+ views writing LinkedIn for 100+ founders. what actually works:
1. post from the founder, not the brand page. people buy from people. the brand page is middle and bottom of funnel, the founder is top
2. every post must make the founder look likable or competent. if it does neither, cut it
3. treat content like product. ship it, measure it, iterate. content is product, product is content
4. if its a value based post write like youre giving away value that has to be screenshottable. thats the bar ask yourself before posting would my reader screenshot and share this to someone?

item.title: X's internal rulebook just leaked. There's a label in it called "llm_slop_post", and you'd…
item.description:
X's internal rulebook just leaked. There's a label in it called "llm_slop_post", and you'd never know you had it.
LinkedIn is building the same thing, and over a million people have already voted on who gets it.
On X the flag sits on your post for 30 days. LinkedIn shipped its version in July, a "Seems like AI slop" button. Every platform is trying to keep AI slop off its site right now, so I'd expect them to copy each other quickly.
Honestly, the algorithm is the smaller problem for me. Comments are often where people meet you first, so I'd rather not put my name to anything I couldn't defend in person. Nothing says "I value you" quite like "Great insights, thanks for sharing!", and I find it hard to buy from someone who couldn't reply to me as a human.
Half my job is helping founders sound like themselves on here, so this one's a bit personal.
Has anyone changed how they comment since AI got this good?

item.title: Anthropic just posted a job paying up to $570,000 for the role I think every company will …
item.description:
Anthropic just posted a job paying up to $570,000 for the role I think every company will need in the next few years.
It's called GTM Narrative Lead, and it's a proper mix of art and science. You write the story and the deck yourself, and then you're expected to prove they work by tracking how often the key messages turn up in real deals.
Most companies still split that into two people, a writer and someone with a dashboard, who mostly meet in the quarterly review. We've been building Draper so one team does both.
I started as an engineer at Goldman, then grew a burger shop to 3,000 reviews at 4.9 with no ad spend, just by telling its story in public. Storytelling took me a long time to learn properly, and the engineer in me only really got into it once I worked out you could test it.
Since September we've been tying our clients' posts to their real sales conversations, so we know which stories are reaching the people on live deals.
I think a lot of companies will be hiring for this soon, whatever they end up calling it.
Is anyone else seeing roles like this pop up outside AI companies?

item.title: 3 WEIRD things my dad has done that I still can't explain: 1. He won a khodu at a mosque a…
item.description:
3 WEIRD things my dad has done that I still can't explain:
1. He won a khodu at a mosque auction
A couple of years ago my local mosque auctioned a khodu (a giant bottle gourd, for the non-Bengalis) after Jummah to raise money for building a new mosque. My dad won it and held it up like a trophy. The photo says the rest.
2. He flew fresh salmon into Bangladesh
On one trip back home he bought these huge polystyrene boxes, filled them with fresh salmon and ice, and checked them in like normal suitcases. Most people bring fish out of Bangladesh. My dad brought it in, and I still have no idea how we got away with it.
3. He sent me to A&E with head lice medicine
When I was a kid he gave me head lice medicine instead of cough medicine (by accident, obviously) and I ended up in A&E.
He's been in food for over 20 years.
Last year a customer brought her parents to our burger shop, and he disappeared into the kitchen and came back with two tiramisu for them. He'd never met them before.
That one I can explain.
